scope: Independent source review and focused replay of the qualification-client lifetime controls

findings_resolved.resolution: The model now selects the actual caller or owned-copy bytes for each region and derives error 777 from memcmp; the mode flag no longer directly determines the return code.
The overwrite helper uses volatile unsigned char stores over each live caller region.

accepted_properties: Every overwrite completes after prepare returns and before finish is invoked. All caller allocations remain live during the readback.
The actual qualification client is included by the C control, preserving the exercised call sequence.
The fixture verifies all observed caller bytes are zero at finish, then compares selected owned/borrowed bytes to the original copies.
The Python control covers 30 combinations: two optimization levels, open/reopen, each individual borrowed region and the owned case.
Compiler diagnostics and runtime stdout/stderr/exit results are checked exactly.
The guard-page routine remains exercised in every case.
claim_boundary: This additional control validates the qualification harness and its owned/borrowed models. It is not a new execution of the production SDK, and the explicit Windows skip is not counted as Windows platform evidence. Existing installed platform qualification remains the runtime evidence.
